rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭāghūt is formed from ṭughyān with the lām moved before the ʿayn, like malakūt and raḥamūt.
rows.anchor: فعلوت من الطغيان كالملكوت والرحموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term denotes Satan or devils; its verbal noun form intensifies the sense, naming Satan as sheer transgression, and its restricted use marks the referent.
rows.anchor: أطلقت على الشيطان أو الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant has the plural al-ṭawāghīt, and the intended referent here is plural.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( الطواغيت ) { أن يعبدوها } بدل من الطاغوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that they worship it is an appositive of inclusion explaining al-ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: { أن يعبدوها } بدل من الطاغوت بدل الاشتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glad tidings are reward, conveyed in revelation by the messengers and by angels at death and resurrection; compare 10:64 and 57:12.
rows.anchor: هي البشارة بالثواب ، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: My servants means those who shunned idolatry and turned to God; the overt noun replaces a pronoun to specify that they must possess the following quality.
rows.anchor: وإنما أراد بهم أن يكونوا مع الاجتناب والإنابة على هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are discerning in religion, distinguishing good from better and choosing the more excellent option.
rows.anchor: أن يكونوا نقادا في الدين يميزون بين الحسن والأحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When duty competes with recommendation they choose duty; between the permissible and recommended they choose the latter for greater divine reward.
rows.anchor: اختاروا الواجب ، وكذلك المباح والندب ، حراصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The principle also covers choosing the most firmly supported and best evidenced school of law after examination.
rows.anchor: واختيار أثبتها على السبك وأقواها عند السبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He warns against blind imitation, illustrating it with a poet’s image of a tethered camel that simply follows.
rows.anchor: ولا تكن مثل عير قيد فانقادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that they hear the Qur’an and other speech, then follow the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: يستمعون القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they hear God’s commands and choose the better course, such as forgiveness over retaliation and discreet charity over public charity (2:237, 2:271).
rows.anchor: ونحو القصاص والعفو ، والانتصار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this describes a person who hears good and bad in a gathering, recounts the best, and withholds the rest.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هو الرجل يجلس مع القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some stop after give good news to My servants and begin those who listen as a nominative subject, with those are as its predicate.
rows.anchor: ومن الوقفة من يقف على : فبشر عبادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rooms are upper chambers, some built above others.
rows.anchor: غرف من فوقها غرف } علالي بعضها فوق بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Built means constructed and finished like earthly houses.
rows.anchor: أنها بنيت بناء المنازل التي على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rivers run beneath the chambers just as they do beneath earthly houses, with no distinction between upper and lower levels.
rows.anchor: كما تجري تحت المنازل ، من غير تفاوت بين العلو والسفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise is an emphatic verbal noun, since saying they have rooms already conveys that God promised them.
rows.anchor: وعد الله } مصدر مؤكد ؛ لأن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is for people and their needs, to bring warning and good news that strengthen motives to choose obedience over sin.
rows.anchor: لأجلهم ولأجل حاجتهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no need of their response: the person who chooses guidance benefits himself, while the person who chooses error harms himself.
rows.anchor: فمن اختار الهدي فقد نفع نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is not charged with forcing people into guidance; moral responsibility rests on choice, not compulsion.
rows.anchor: فإن التكليف مبني على الاختيار دون الإجبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-anfus means whole persons; taking them means causing death by removing the health and integrity that let their parts live, sense, and perceive.
rows.anchor: وتوفيها : إماتتها ، وهو أن يسلب ما هي به حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is like the removal of a person’s whole self when the health of its parts is taken away.
rows.anchor: هو أن يسلب ما هي به حية حساسة دراكة : من صحة أجزائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes the souls of sleepers as they sleep, likening them to the dead because they cannot distinguish or act; compare 6:60.
rows.anchor: يريد ويتوفى الأنفس التي لم تمت في منامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleepers cannot distinguish or act, just as the dead cannot.
rows.anchor: حيث لا يميزون ولا يتصرفون ، كما أن الموتى كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God retains the souls whose true death He has decreed and does not restore them to life at that time.
rows.anchor: الأنفس { التي قضى عليها الموت } الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He releases the sleeping soul until the appointed time of its death.
rows.anchor: الأخرى } النائمة إلى أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative distinguishes the life-and-motion spirit from the soul of intellect and discernment, saying sleep takes the latter while breathing continues through the former.
rows.anchor: يتوفى الأنفس يستوفيها ويقضيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says a person has a discerning soul and a spirit for breathing and movement; God takes the soul in sleep but not the spirit.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في ابن آدم : نفس وروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects that distinction: the verse predicates death and sleep of the same whole person, while the proposed faculties are not themselves described as dying or sleeping.
rows.anchor: والصحيح ما ذكرت أولا ، لأن الله عز وعلا علق التوفي والموت والمنام جميعا بالأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taking, retaining, and releasing of souls are signs of God’s power and knowledge for people who reflect and draw a lesson.
rows.anchor: إن في توفي الأنفس مائتة ونائمة وإمساكها وإرسالها إلى أجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the phrase with passive voice: death was decreed against it.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( قضي عليها الموت ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who exceeded bounds against themselves are people who committed sins excessively.
rows.anchor: جنوا عليها بالإسراف في المعاصي والغلو فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with the nūn bearing fatḥa, kasra, or ḍamma.
rows.anchor: قرىء : بفتح النون وكسرها وضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness is conditional on repentance; the Qur’an repeats this condition, and as one coherent discourse cannot contradict itself, it applies even where unstated.
rows.anchor: يعني بشرط التوبة ، وقد تكرر ذكر هذا الشرط في القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd adds for whom He wills; al-Zamakhsharī says this means those who repent, since divine will follows wisdom and justice.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن عباس وابن مسعود : ( يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفاطمة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: Another reported reading attributed to the Prophet and Fāṭima adds and He does not care.
rows.anchor: في قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفاطمة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of concern is compared with the Qur’anic denial of fear in 91:15.
rows.anchor: ونظير نفي المبالاة نفي الخوف في قوله تعالى : { ولا يخاف عقباها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says Meccans asked how they could emigrate after worshipping idols and killing a person God forbade killing, since they thought Muḥammad said they could not be forgiven.
rows.anchor: قال أهل مكة : يزعم محمد أن من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس

rows.speaker: عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد
rows.claim: Another occasion report concerns ʿAyyāsh b. Abī Rabīʿa, al-Walīd b. al-Walīd, and others who accepted Islam, were tortured into apostasy, then received this verse through ʿUmar and returned to Islam and emigrated.
rows.anchor: أسلم عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر معهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further opinion says the verse was revealed about Waḥshī, who killed Ḥamza.
rows.anchor: نزلت في وحشي قاتل حمزة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prized the verse above the world and all it contains; when asked whether it included one who associated partners, he affirmed that it did, repeating this three times.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 970 ) ( ما أحب أن لي الدنيا وما فيها بهذه الآية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no doubt about it means the Hour must certainly come, since recompense is inevitable.
rows.anchor: لا بد من مجيئها ولا محالة ، وليس بمرتاب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not believe means they do not affirm the Hour.
rows.anchor: { لا يؤمنون } لا يصدقون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here call on Me means worship Me; the following clause confirms this, and the Qur’an often uses supplication for worship.
rows.anchor: والدعاء بمعنى العبادة كثير في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here response means reward; Mujāhid glosses the verse worship Me, I will reward you.
rows.anchor: في تفسير مجاهد : اعبدوني أثبكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to act and rejoice, since God is bound to answer believers who do good and increase them from His bounty.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن وقد سئل عنها : اعملوا وأبشروا

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: When al-Thawrī was asked to pray, he replied that abandoning sins is prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن الثوري أنه قيل له : ادع الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that if obedience to God occupies a servant instead of supplication, God gives him something better than what He gives those who ask.
rows.anchor: إذا شغل عبدي طاعتي عن الدعاء ، أعطيته أفضل

rows.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
rows.claim: Al-Nuʿmān b. Bashīr reports that the Prophet called supplication worship and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وروى النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنه ، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse can mean supplicate to Me and I will answer; worship here means supplication, one of worship’s best avenues.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد الدعاء والاستجابة على ظاهرهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says supplication is the best worship.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أفضل العبادة الدعاء

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says this community received three privileges given only to a sent prophet: witness over people (2:143), freedom from religious hardship (5:6), and the promise that prayer will be answered.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب : أعطى الله هذه الأمة ثلاث خلال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as affirm My oneness and I will forgive you, explaining supplication as worship and worship as monotheism.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : وحدوني أغفر لكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase threatens those who arrogantly reject worship with entering Hell in abasement; dākhirīn means humbled.
rows.anchor: إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in He created them can refer to night, day, sun, and moon, since nonrational plurals take feminine agreement.
rows.anchor: الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر ؛ لأن حكم جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the antecedent is the implied plural signs in the phrase among His signs.
rows.anchor: قال { ومن ءاياته } كن في معنى الآيات

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī places the prostration at you worship; this matches Masrūq’s report from ʿAbd Allāh because the prostration word appears just before it.
rows.anchor: عند الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى : { تعبدون } وهي رواية مسروق عن عبد الله

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa places the prostration at they do not tire, as the completion of the meaning; Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, and Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib are also cited for this location.
rows.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله : يسأمون ؛ لأنها تمام المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people prostrated to sun and moon like the Sabians, claiming to intend God through them; they were told to abandon this intermediary and prostrate sincerely to God, even if already monotheists.
rows.anchor: لعل ناسا منهم كانوا يسجدون للشمس والقمر كالصابئين في عبادتهم الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they refuse and insist on an intermediary, leave them to it: God has sincere, near servants who glorify Him day and night.
rows.anchor: فإن استكبروا } ولم يمتثلوا ما أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With your Lord expresses nearness, status, and honor, not physical location.
rows.anchor: عند ربك } عبارة عن الزلفى والمكانة والكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has the yāʾ in they do not tire with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لا يسأمون ) بكسر الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has and He constricts; God gives a servant wealth if He knows that is better, and otherwise makes him poor.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ويقدر ) { إنه بكل شىء عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed for this community the religion of Noah, Muḥammad, and the prophets between them.
rows.anchor: دين نوح ومحمد ومن بينهما من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared prescription is to uphold Islam: God’s oneness and obedience, belief in messengers and scriptures, the Day of Judgment, and what makes a person Muslim.
rows.anchor: إقامة دين الإسلام الذي هو توحيد الله وطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common command concerns Islam’s fundamentals, not separate laws tailored to different communities and circumstances (5:48).
rows.anchor: الشرائع التي هي مصالح الأمم على حسب أحوالها ، فإنها مختلفة متفاوتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause to uphold the religion may be accusative as an appositive to the object of prescribed, or nominative as a new explanation of what was prescribed.
rows.anchor: { أن أقيموا } إما نصب بدل من مفعول شرع والمعطوفين عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the explanatory resumption with the parallel formulation at 21:92.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { إن هاذه أمتكم * أمة واحدة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is great upon the associators means establishing God’s religion is weighty and difficult for them.
rows.anchor: كبر على المشركين } عظم عليهم وشق عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yajtabī means to draw and gather toward the religion; God does so by enabling and supporting those who benefit from His guidance and receive His gentleness.
rows.anchor: الضمير للدين بالتوفيق والتسديد { من يشاء } من ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes a continuing past condition: the people habitually behaved this way.
rows.anchor: حكاية حال ماضية مستمرة ، أي : كانوا على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of prior peoples comforts the Messenger over his people’s mockery.
rows.anchor: تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن استهزاء قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in stronger than them refers to the extravagant peoples; the address shifts from them to the Messenger as God reports their fate.
rows.anchor: للقوم المسرفين ، لأنه صرف الخطاب عنهم إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples’ extraordinary stories recur in the Qur’an as cautionary examples; this promises support to the Messenger and threatens his opponents.
rows.anchor: ذكر قصتهم وحالهم العجيبة التي حقها أن تسير مسير المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pagans attribute creation of the heavens and earth to the one described as Mighty and Knowing.
rows.anchor: لينسبن خلقها إلى الذي هذه أوصافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words We revived a dead land and the descriptions following the pagans’ admission are God’s speech, not theirs.
rows.anchor: هو من قول الله لا من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain comes in an amount that keeps lands and people safe rather than causing a flood.
rows.anchor: بمقدار يسلم معه البلاد والعباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-azwāj means kinds or classes.
rows.anchor: الازواج } الأصناف { ما تركبون } أي تركبونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Arabic says one rides livestock directly but rides in ships with a preposition, the direct construction prevails here as the stronger verb pattern.
rows.anchor: غلب المتعدي بغير واسطة ، لقوته على المتعدي بواسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their backs means the backs of the things people ride, both ships and livestock.
rows.anchor: على ظهور ما تركبونه وهو الفلك والأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the blessing means acknowledging and esteeming it inwardly, then praising God for it aloud.
rows.anchor: أن يذكروها في قلوبهم معترفين بها مستعظمين لها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said In God’s name when putting a foot in the stirrup, then praised God and recited through we shall return after mounting, adding three takbīrs and three declarations of oneness.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They said that when boarding a ship one should say In God’s name is its course and anchorage (11:41).
rows.anchor: إذا ركب في السفينة قال : { بسم الله مجراها

words: وَتَقُولُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī corrected a man who recited the glorification but omitted praise, reminding him to remember God’s blessing.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما أنه رأى رجلا يركب دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correction illustrates the early community’s care for fine details of religious etiquette.
rows.anchor: من حسن مراعاتهم لآداب الله ومحافظتهم على دقيقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqrinīn means able to master something; Arabic uses aqrana for having the capacity to do it.
rows.anchor: مطيقين . يقال : أقرن الشيء ، إذا أطاقه

rows.speaker: ابن هرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Hurmā’s verse uses aqrant to mean being able to bear the beloved’s rejection and estrangement.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هرمة : وأقرنت ما حملتني ولقلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying sense is to find something a match or companion: a difficult beast cannot be paired with a weak rider.
rows.anchor: وجده قرينته وما يقرن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads muqarrinīn with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( مقرنين ) والمعنى واحد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riding is dangerous: falls, runaway animals, or shipwreck may cause death, so riders should remember their certain return and prepare through reform.
rows.anchor: فلما كان الركوب مباشرة أمر مخطر ، واتصالا بسبب من أسباب التلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He warns against pleasure rides with wine and instruments, where riders remember Satan and obey him instead of preparing for death.
rows.anchor: أواني الخمر والمعازف ، فلا يزالون يسقون حتى تميل طلاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports hearing of a ruler who drank throughout a month-long journey and only became sober after reaching his destination, unaware of the trip.
rows.anchor: وقد بلغني أن بعض السلاطين ركب وهو يشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation is that riders remember mounting the funeral bier.
rows.anchor: يذكرون عند الركوب ركوب الجنازة

none: The segment quotes verses without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before it may refer to the Qur’an or to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: { من قبله } للقرآن أو الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They attribute associating partners with God to His will without knowledge; the rhetorical question asks whether a prior revealed book actually taught them to ascribe disbelief and vice to God.
rows.anchor: ألصقوا عبادة غير الله بمشيئة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage denies they have revelation to rely on; their only argument is that their fathers followed a way.
rows.anchor: أم آتيناهم كتابا قبل هذا الكتاب نسبنا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no revealed proof; their only argument is that they found their fathers following a way.
rows.anchor: لا حجة لهم يستمسكون بها إلا قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads imma with kasra; both forms derive from the root of intending or aiming.
rows.anchor: وكلتاهما من الأم وهو القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umma means a way that people intend and follow, by analogy with a destination one sets out for.
rows.anchor: الطريقة التي تؤم ، أي : تقصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the phrase to mean a blessing or a good condition.
rows.anchor: وقيل : على نعمة وحالة حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase upon a way, and we follow can make the following clause the predicate of inna, or link the prepositional phrase to guided.
rows.anchor: خبر إن . أو الظرف صلة لمهتدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse summarizes the sūra and reminds them through the clear Book.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم بالكتاب المبين ( فإنما يسرناه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He made the Qur’an easy by revealing it in the Prophet’s Arabic so his people could understand and remember.
rows.anchor: سهلناه ، حيث أنزلناه عربيا بلسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wait means wait to see what befalls them; they are lying in wait for misfortune to befall the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فارتقب } فانتظر ما يحل بهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that one who recites Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Dukhān at night will awaken with 70,000 angels seeking forgiveness for him.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1019 ) ( من قرأ سورة حم الدخان

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another report promises forgiveness by morning for one who recites the sūra mentioning the Smoke on Friday night.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : ( 1020 ) ( من قرأ سورة حم التي ذكر فيها الدخان في ليلة جمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of Qāf and the glorious Qur’an parallels 38:1–2 exactly because the two passages share the same style.
rows.anchor: نحوه في { ص والقرءان ذي الذكر * بل الذين كفروا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majīd means glorious and superior to other books; whoever understands the Qur’an and acts on it is honored by God and people, since the book derives its quality from God, the Majīd.
rows.anchor: ذو المجد والشرف على غيره من الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their amazement at a warner from among them is misplaced: they knew his standing, honesty, and fairness, and such a man could only sincerely warn his people of approaching harm.
rows.anchor: لم يكن إلا ناصحا لقومه مترفرفا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person warns when ordinary danger approaches, it is all the more necessary to warn of the greatest dangers and ultimate calamities.
rows.anchor: إذا علم أن مخوفا أظلهم ، لزمه أن ينذرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of resurrection is especially absurd: they acknowledge God’s power to originate all things, admit the first creation, and reason requires recompense.
rows.anchor: مع علمهم بقدرة الله تعالى على خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He replaces the pronoun with disbelievers to mark the gravity of their unbelief, focusing on their rejection of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وضع الكافرون موضع الضمير للشهادة على أنهم في قولهم هذا مقدمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to the return to life after death.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الرجع ؛ وإذا منصوب بمضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time adverb is governed by an implied verb: will we be returned when we have died and decayed?
rows.anchor: معناه : أحين نموت ونبلى نرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Far means beyond customary experience and what the mind considers plausible.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : بعيد من الوهم والعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively rajʿ means the returned answer, making this God’s comment that their denial of resurrection is itself outlandish.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الرجع بمعنى المرجوع . وهو الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has idhā in declarative form rather than a question; it is understood as when we die after we have returned, as the following phrase indicates.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( إذا متنا ) على لفظ الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If rajʿ means the returned answer, the time adverb is governed by the resurrection matter implied by the word warner.
rows.anchor: ما دل عليه المنذر من المنذر به ، وهو البعث

none: The segment contains only a quoted verse, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madadnāhā means that God spread and leveled the earth.
rows.anchor: مددناها } دحوناها { رواسي } جبالا ثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are fixed masses; without them the earth would tilt.
rows.anchor: جبالا ثوابت لولا هي لتكفأت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj here means every kind or class.
rows.anchor: من كل زوج } من كل صنف { بهيج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahīj describes what delights because of its beauty.
rows.anchor: بهيج } يبتهج به لحسنه { تبصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is made a lesson and reminder for every servant who turns to God and reflects on its wonders.
rows.anchor: لتبصر به وتذكر كل { عبد منيب } راجع إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nominative reading takes the creation itself to be a lesson and reminder.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( تبصرة وذكرى ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessed rain is rain rich in benefits.
rows.anchor: ماء مباركا } كثير المنافع { وحب الحصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grain is the crop meant to be harvested and eaten as staple food, such as wheat and barley.
rows.anchor: وحب الحصيد } وحب الزرع الذي من شأنه أن يحصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāsiqāt means palms growing tall into the sky.
rows.anchor: طوالا في السماء : وفي قراءة رسول الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A reading attributed to the Prophet has bāṣiqāt with ṣād replacing sīn because of the following qāf.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : باصقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naḍīd means heaped or layered; it may describe the abundant overlapping spathes or the large amount of fruit within them.
rows.anchor: نضيد } منضود بعضه فوق بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizqan may mean We grew them as provision, since growing entails provision, or be a purpose clause: We grew them to provide for people.
rows.anchor: رزقا } على أنبتناها رزقا ، لأن الإنبات في معنى الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as God revives this dead land, He will bring people to life after death.
rows.anchor: كذالك الخروج } كما حييت هذه البلدة الميتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in thus is nominative as the subject of an equative clause.
rows.anchor: والكاف في محل الرفع على الابتداء
